newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ sees c/a deficit at NZ$6.2 bln by March 1999.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ sees c/a deficit at NZ$6.2 bln by March 1999.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand in its six monthly economic projections on Thursday forecast the current account deficit to reach NZ$6.167 billion in the year to March 1999, or 5.9 percent of nominal GDP.
The forecast compares with the previous forecast in September when the deficit was forecast to reach a peak of NZ$4.005 billion in the year to March 1998, 4.2 percent of nominal GDP.

The bank said it projected the current account deficit to reach NZ$5.467 billion in the year to March 1997, or 5.8 percent of nominal GDP, and $5.359 billion the following year. The deficit is picked to fall slightly in 2000 to $6.040 billion, 5.6 percent of GDP.
Statistics New Zealand said the current account deficit was NZ$4.2 billion in the September 1996 year, 4.6 percent of GDP.
The bank said the projected deficit of nearly 6 percent of GDP would be around seven percent if migrants' cash transfers were excluded.
The bank said that a deficit of this magnitude was unlikely to be sustained indefitely.

"At some point, adjustment is likely to occur either voluntarily (in the form of an increase in household and firm savings) or through the external constraints provided by financial markets (in the form of a substantial capital outflow as investors seek to protect themselves from the inevitable depreciation of the real exchange rate)."
The bank said there was a clear risk such an adjustment could occur during the three-year forecast period.
Such an adjustment would mean a substantial rebalancing of monetary conditions.
